rationale: Blowfish is a compact, extremely hot cryptographic kernel dominated by bitwise logic, modular additions, and heavy access to static tables (S-boxes and the P-array) inside a 16-round Feistel loop, with essentially no indirect-call-rich code. SUB gets the highest priority because arithmetic/logic substitution maps directly onto the cipher's XOR/add mix at near-zero cost; IGV is prioritized nearly as highly since virtually all of the cipher state lives in global/static arrays, so indirecting table references obfuscates the most informative data flow cheaply. FLA and BCF receive strong security/diversity weights to destroy the clean per-round control-flow signature that reverse engineers use to locate and lift the Feistel network, with runtime/size weights held at moderate levels so the hot decrypt/encrypt loop is not over-transformed. IBR is kept at a moderate weight with an elevated CorrectnessRisk acknowledgment: indirect branching is powerful against static analysis but adds real dispatch overhead in a tight loop, so it should only attach to functions whose features genuinely support it. SPLIT is cheap and improves the coverage of FLA/BCF/IBR, so it is enabled as a force multiplier. ICALL is effectively deprioritized (low security weight): blowfish exposes almost no call sites worth indirecting, so its weight is low enough that the selector will rarely fire it, though it is retained for any dispatch-like helpers.
